title: Multi-SDK deprecation-safe upgrade: auth/retry parity, ergonomic streaming migrations and version bumps
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Bump Python/TS/Go SDKs with compatibility shims and migration helpers. Non-breaking aliases preserved for 2 releases. See migration guide in SDK root for minimal code changes.
description:
Context & goal:
We observed subtle behavior drift across SDKs after the last round of retry/reauth changes: different default retry windows, slightly different streaming iterator semantics (prefetch vs pause behavior), and inconsistent deprecation signals when credential schemas changed. This PR's goal is to converge the Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs on a single, deprecation-safe upgrade path: unify auth/reauth presets, align default retry timelines (with adaptive jitter), normalize async streaming ergonomics, and bump versions with automated migration helpers. The approach emphasizes backward compatibility-first: runtime shims + opt-in stricter behavior behind feature flags for one release.

Summary of changes (single-line commit highlights):
- chore(sdk): bump py 2.x -> 3.0.0-alpha / ts 1.x -> 2.0.0 / go v1.x -> v2.0.0-preview
- feat(auth): introduce CredAdapter abstraction with language-specific adapters and a shared semantic contract
- feat(retries): add adaptive-retry-presets with coordinated default windows and an explicit RetryProfile enum
- feat(stream): provide PausableAsyncIterator (py/ts) and StreamHandle (go) with consistent semantics; add migration helpers
- docs(migration): add SDK_MIGRATION.md with codemod examples and recommended timeline

Files changed (high level):
- sdk/python/redwood/__init__.py (version bump, new CredAdapter, deprecation warnings)
- sdk/python/redwood/streaming/iterators.py (PausableAsyncIterator + tests)
- sdk/python/redwood/retry/presets.py (RetryProfile + adaptive algorithm)
- sdk/python/tools/migrations.py (simple codemod to adapt old session calls)
- sdk/typescript/src/auth/credAdapter.ts (TS CredAdapter surface + README snippet)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream/pullGenerator.ts (generator wrapper + pause/resume semantics)
- sdk/typescript/fixtures/migration-example.ts
- sdk/go/credentials/adapter.go (CredAdapter interface + shim impl)
- sdk/go/stream/handle.go (StreamHandle with Pause/Resume semantics)
- sdk/common/retry_profiles.json (source-of-truth profiles used to generate language presets)

Testing & CI:
- Unit test suites added/updated in each sdk: Python (pytest), TypeScript (vitest), Go (go test).
- Integration: end-to-end streaming test that runs a simulated token server and asserts consistent pause/resume behavior across SDK clients.
- CI flaky tests: two TS streaming tests initially flaked on Windows runners; we pinned to Node 20 in the matrix and re-ran. Final CI state: all checks green.

Review conversation (high level transcript snippets):
- Jun Park (reviewer): "Please ensure we don't silently drop user-defined RetryProfile values. Also, add an env flag to opt-out of adaptive jitter during canarying."
- Author (Ava): "Added explicit mapping for legacy profile names and introduced REDWOOD_ADAPTIVE_RETRY=false to disable adaptive jitter at runtime. Documented in SDK_MIGRATION.md."
- Riley Chen: "The Go StreamHandle pause logic may block if caller forgets to Resume; can we add a safety timeout and stronger docs?"
- Ava: "Added a warning-level timer that logs if Resume isn't called within 30s and added an ergonomic helper StreamHandle.SafeResume(). Also added test coverage."
- Marta Gómez: "Docs look good; please include short codemod examples for the most common 3 migration patterns."
- Ava: "Included a Python codemod and a TS code snippet; queued a follow-up ticket to provide a Go migration script (ENG-1314)."

Compatibility & migration plan:
- No immediate forced breaking changes. The new CredAdapter surface accepts old credentials via the included LegacyCredShim for two releases. We mark the old auth.Session.* methods as deprecated with runtime warnings.
- Migration helpers included: python tools/migrations.py, typescript migration examples, go shim with clear TODOs. The SDK root contains SDK_MIGRATION.md with step-by-step instructions and examples.
- Versioning: semantic-major bump to signal the presence of new ergonomics but defaulting to compatibility. We coordinated with the product release team for a staged rollout: first publish pre-release packages, then GA after ~3 weeks of telemetry.

Performance and perf notes:
- Retry changes include a small perf win in high-error tails due to compacted jitter; measured ~3-5% lower average token latency under 95th percentile in local bench harness.
- Streaming pause/resume adds negligible CPU overhead; memory usage slightly reduced because generator prefetch window is controllable via SDK config.

Follow-ups and tickets created:
- ENG-1314: Add Go codemod/migration script (assigned to @marta)
- ENG-1320: Add telemetry to report which RetryProfile is in use by default for customers on the first GA week
- SUP-4421: Customer-facing support note templating for SDK upgrade

Merge outcome:
- Squash merge into main. Commit message kept high-level summary and included link to SDK_MIGRATION.md. Release artifacts: py wheel (3.0.0a1), npm packages (2.0.0-rc.1), go module tagged v2.0.0-preview.

Notes for maintainers:
- Keep LegacyCredShim for 2 minor releases; add a follow-up to schedule its removal on a clearly documented date.
- Monitor canary telemetry for RetryProfile adoption and streaming error spikes.

If you want to exercise the migration helpers locally: see sdk/python/README.md and run python tools/migrations.py --dry-run against a sample codebase.
